title: Policy Learning with $\alpha$-Expected Welfare
abstract: arXiv:2505.00256v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper proposes an optimal policy that targets the average welfare of the worst-off $\alpha$-fraction of the post-treatment outcome distribution. We refer to this policy as the $\alpha$-Expected Welfare Maximization ($\alpha$-EWM) rule, where $\alpha \in (0,1]$ denotes the size of the subpopulation of interest. The $\alpha$-EWM rule interpolates between the expected welfare ($\alpha=1$) and the Rawlsian welfare ($\alpha\rightarrow 0$). For $\alpha\in (0,1)$, an $\alpha$-EWM rule can be interpreted as a distributionally robust EWM rule that allows the target population to have a different distribution than the study population. Using the dual formulation of our $\alpha$-expected welfare function, we propose a debiased estimator for the optimal policy and establish its asymptotic upper regret bounds. tldr: 提出了一种新的政策学习规则，通过调整参数$\alpha$在期望福利与罗尔斯福利之间平滑过渡，并提供了去偏估计和渐近推断方法，以实现对最差子群体平均福利的优化。
en_tdlr: Proposes a novel policy learning rule that smoothly interpolates between expected and Rawlsian welfare via parameter $\alpha$, with debiased estimation and asymptotic inference for optimizing the average welfare of the worst-off subpopulation.
